source_anchor.value: You can’t walk into a gallery without learning about some subcultural genius or longlost creative you’ve never heard of.

disturbance.value: The review repeatedly frames discovery as a physical act of wandering — following your nose, walking into galleries, sniffing something out across a sprawl of venues from City Art Gallery to Calton Hill to Jupiter Artland — yet it never registers that this mobile, spontaneous mode of encounter is itself a condition of entry, not a neutral given. A festival that celebrates the marginalised and unseen assumes a reader-body that can freely cross the whole city to do the seeing.
disturbance.note: what in the evidence does not fit the ordinary explanation

hidden_mechanism.value: The festival's entire discovery premise is coded as an ambulatory act — following your nose across venues, walking in, sniffing something out — so the review's own prose enacts a navigation model that presumes a spontaneous mobile body, meaning the 'unheralded' it celebrates is filtered through an access architecture that quietly pre-selects who can do the uncovering.

reader_contract.value: Anyone who has ever felt vaguely guilty at an art festival — dragged from venue to venue, lectured about geniuses they've never heard of, told they're a bastard for not knowing — will recognise the exhaustion and the pleasure in this review, which is funny and honest about what it's actually like to be a body walking through too much art in one city.

source_excerpt.value: You’ve just got to follow your nose and hope you sniff out something you like.

editorial_note.value: The review's own prescribed method of encounter is bodily and ambulatory, treating spontaneous physical wandering as the natural way to access the festival's hidden stories.

source_excerpt.value: There are curated displays, satellite exhibitions, performances, off-site projects, and it’s impossible to figure out how any of it fits together.

editorial_note.value: The dispersed, off-site structure is exactly what demands the mobile body the review presumes, and the difficulty of navigation is registered as personal confusion rather than an access condition.

source_excerpt.value: Over among the horses and goats of Jupiter Artland

editorial_note.value: The physical spread of venues to a rural sculpture park shows how far the discovering body is expected to travel to complete the festival.

source_excerpt.value: By the time you’re done with Edinburgh art festival you’ll have uncovered so many hidden stories you’ll feel like Columbo.

editorial_note.value: The discovery premise is framed as an active detective-like uncovering performed by the visitor, foregrounding who is doing the uncovering.

source_excerpt.value: Richard Maguire at Collective Gallery at the top of Calton Hill

editorial_note.value: A concrete geographic waypoint the reader can be walked to; part of a chain of named locations the review physically traverses.

source_excerpt.value: She captured protests and action groups operating out of living rooms and town halls; people living in hostels and housing schemes, skinheads, labourers, Hare Krishnas, Indians, Jamaicans, white and black.

editorial_note.value: Sandra George moving through Craigmillar as a semi-outsider documentarian is itself a vivid enactment of who does the discovering and from what position — a human thread the reader can follow.

source_excerpt.value: A figure in a Georgian wig grins menacingly at you as you enter, a red plasticine smile plastered across his face.

editorial_note.value: A vivid, physically encountered object that lets the reader watch the writer walk in and be confronted, dramatising the ambulatory encounter model.

source_excerpt.value: The whole thing could do with some more ambition, some bigger names, some starrier attractions. And it’s all a bit worthy and lecture-y, like you’re getting told off in every gallery you enter.

editorial_note.value: The tension between celebrating the unheralded and feeling scolded by it gives the piece its central live contradiction to carry the reader.

source_excerpt.value: “You’ve never heard of this previously undiscovered marginalised artist? You bastard!”

editorial_note.value: A sharp comic line that can anchor the reader emotionally in the experience of being a wandering, lectured visitor.
